name: @brandcloud/motion antipatterns
description: Motion tells that make interfaces feel AI generated, with detection heuristics and fixes. Same shape as @brandcloud/antipatterns rules.json (category MOT). AP-MOT-01 to 09 match its ids and meaning; AP-MOT-20 onward are new from @brandcloud/motion. detect.kind is dom, css (static stylesheet scan), or runtime (needs a live page over time); checks a detector does not implement should be reported as manual.

rules.title: Everything fades up on scroll
rules.description: Most sections or cards start invisible and rise into place as they scroll into view.
rules.whyAI: Generators wrap every block in the same whileInView or AOS entrance. It hides content from fast scrollers, print and screenshots, and tells the visitor nothing.
rules.heuristic: Four or more elements in one page start with opacity 0 plus a translate and change on intersection (data-aos, .reveal, whileInView, IntersectionObserver class toggles).
rules.fix: Content visible by default. At most one or two reveals per page where arrival means something (a result, a proof figure). Use @brandcloud/motion reveal() which never hides content without JS and skips movement for reduced motion.

rules.title: Staggered entrance on every card
rules.description: Sibling cards animate in one after another with growing delays on scroll.
rules.whyAI: The stagger is the default polish a model adds to any repeated element. It slows reading and repeats on every list.
rules.heuristic: Three or more siblings with incrementing animation-delay or transition-delay that run on scroll rather than after a user action.
rules.fix: Show lists at once. Stagger only when a user action produces the list (menu opens, results load), capped by stagger.maxItems and budget.maxStaggerTotal (300ms total).

rules.title: Hover lift and scale on every card
rules.description: Every card, image and tile lifts, scales or tilts on hover, including ones that are not links.
rules.whyAI: Hover lift is a free default in UI kits. When everything moves, nothing signals what is clickable.
rules.heuristic: Three or more non-interactive elements change transform on :hover.
rules.fix: Only interactive things respond to hover, and only on (hover: hover) pointers. Offer tiles may lift 4px (distance.lift) because the whole tile is the action; plain cards do not move.

rules.title: Endless floating and pulsing decoration
rules.description: Badges, icons, blobs or mock UI that float, bob, pulse or rotate forever.
rules.whyAI: Infinite idle loops are the easiest way to make a static layout look busy. They pull the eye from the content and fail WCAG 2.2.2 when they run past five seconds without a pause.
rules.heuristic: Two or more elements with animation-iteration-count: infinite that are not loading indicators.
rules.fix: No idle loops. Infinite animation is for progress only (a spinner while something loads), and it becomes a pulse under reduced motion (.m-spinner).

rules.title: Infinite logo marquee
rules.description: An endlessly scrolling strip of client or partner logos, often logos the business has never worked with.
rules.whyAI: The auto-playing marquee of fake logos is the signature of template landing pages. It is also moving content without a pause control.
rules.heuristic: A horizontally translating, infinitely animated row of four or more images or SVGs.
rules.fix: Show a few real, named clients still, with a short line of what was done for each. If there is no real proof yet, leave it out.

rules.title: Cursor-following glow or spotlight
rules.description: A radial glow, spotlight or blob that follows the pointer across sections or card borders.
rules.whyAI: Spotlight cards and cursor glows came from component galleries and are now pasted everywhere. They do nothing on touch and nothing for meaning.
rules.heuristic: pointermove or mousemove listeners that write a CSS variable or transform used in a radial-gradient background, mask or blurred element.
rules.fix: Remove it. Use real state feedback: hover, focus-visible and pressed states on actual controls.

rules.title: Typewriter or rotating-word headline
rules.description: The headline types itself out, or a word in it keeps swapping.
rules.whyAI: It delays the one sentence that matters and was a stock pattern in AI landing templates. Screen readers may read partial text.
rules.heuristic: The h1 text content changes within the first 1200ms after load, or a caret element blinks inside it.
rules.fix: Static headline, readable in the first frame. Say the one thing plainly.

rules.title: Parallax-scrolling decorative shapes
rules.description: Blobs, grids or shapes that move at a different speed from the page as it scrolls.
rules.whyAI: Parallax decoration is depth with no object. It costs scroll performance and is a common vestibular trigger.
rules.heuristic: Decorative (aria-hidden or empty) elements whose transform changes by 20px or more during a 400px scroll.
rules.fix: Remove decorative layers. If depth is needed, use the tonal light-model gradient and shadows on the real object (buttons, offer tiles).

rules.title: Purposeless spinning 3D hero object
rules.description: A large 3D shape, globe or abstract blob that spins or drifts in the hero with no link to the offer.
rules.whyAI: Spline and Three.js scenes are a one-click way to look premium. With no meaning they are a heavy, battery-draining screensaver.
rules.heuristic: A canvas or 3D embed of 160px or more in the first viewport that animates continuously with no user input.
rules.fix: 3D only when it explains something (a product the user can turn, a logo mark at small size). Lazy-load, pause off screen and in hidden tabs, static image under reduced motion. See the motion-lab turntable.

rules.title: No reduced-motion handling
rules.description: Transforms, parallax, auto-play or scroll effects run the same when the visitor has asked the OS for reduced motion.
rules.whyAI: Generated code adds motion by default and almost never adds the opposite case.
rules.heuristic: Stylesheets contain @keyframes or transform transitions but no prefers-reduced-motion query, and scripts start animations without checking matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').
rules.fix: Import @brandcloud/motion tokens (distances and scales go to zero under reduced motion) and use MotionConfig reducedMotion="user", Reanimated reduceMotion: "system", or prefersReducedMotion() in scripts.

rules.title: Animating layout properties
rules.description: Transitions or keyframes on width, height, top, left, margin or padding.
rules.whyAI: Models reach for the property that describes the change, not the one the browser can animate cheaply. It causes layout on every frame and jank on phones.
rules.heuristic: transition or @keyframes that list width, height, top, right, bottom, left, margin or padding (max-height accordions included).
rules.fix: Animate transform and opacity. For accordions use grid-template-rows 0fr to 1fr, interpolate-size or the details element; for drawers translate.

rules.title: transition: all
rules.description: A blanket transition on every property.
rules.whyAI: It is the default in snippets and UI kits. It animates colour, shadow and layout changes nobody designed and makes theme switches smear.
rules.heuristic: transition: all or transition-property: all in any rule.
rules.fix: List the properties: transform, opacity, filter, and colour only where intended.

rules.title: Slow interface motion
rules.description: Hovers, menus, dialogs and tab changes that take longer than half a second.
rules.whyAI: Long, floaty easing reads as a demo, not a tool. Users wait for the interface instead of the other way round.
rules.heuristic: Transition or animation durations above 500ms on interactive elements (count-up and scroll-linked timelines excepted).
rules.fix: Use the duration tokens: instant 80, fast 140, normal 220, slow 320, slower 480 (page transitions only).

rules.title: Bouncy overshoot on everything
rules.description: Elastic or back easing, or bouncy springs, on menus, dialogs, page transitions and layout.
rules.whyAI: Bounce is the quickest way to make motion feel playful, so generators use it everywhere. On structural UI it feels cheap and unsettled.
rules.heuristic: cubic-bezier with a y value above 1 or below 0, easeOutBack, elastic or bounce easings, or springs with damping ratio below 0.5 on non-delight elements.
rules.fix: Structural motion uses standard, enter, exit or the snappy and gentle springs. spring.bouncy is for one success moment per flow.

rules.title: Scroll hijacking and smooth-scroll libraries
rules.description: The page intercepts the wheel or touch scroll to apply its own inertia, snapping or pinned scenes.
rules.whyAI: Lenis and Locomotive-style scrolling are a stock premium effect. They break the user's own scroll speed, find-in-page, anchor links and assistive tech.
rules.heuristic: Scripts or classes from lenis, locomotive-scroll or similar; wheel listeners with preventDefault; long pinned scroll sections.
rules.fix: Native scrolling. If a section needs scroll-linked motion, use CSS animation-timeline on a small element and keep the scroll itself untouched.

rules.title: Choreographed hero intro
rules.description: The headline, sub-copy, buttons and image arrive in sequence after load, so the first readable frame comes late.
rules.whyAI: Intro timelines look good in a screen recording and badly in real use. They also delay Largest Contentful Paint.
rules.heuristic: The h1 or primary CTA has opacity 0 or an animation-delay above 200ms at first paint.
rules.fix: The hero is static on load. Motion starts with the user: hover, press, scroll, navigation.

rules.title: Animated gradient or mesh background
rules.description: Large backgrounds whose gradient position, hue or mesh shifts continuously.
rules.whyAI: Moving aurora and mesh gradients are a 2024 to 2026 AI landing cliche and break the tonal gradient rule (no hue shift, no light logic).
rules.heuristic: Keyframes that change background-position, background-size or hue-rotate on elements wider than half the viewport.
rules.fix: Still backgrounds. Gradients only as tonal light models on actions and offer tiles, from tokens.

rules.title: Every number counts up
rules.description: All stats, prices or percentages tick up from zero when they appear.
rules.whyAI: Count-ups are a stock dashboard flourish. On prices they look like a gimmick, and screen readers can announce every step.
rules.heuristic: More than one count-up per view, or any count-up on a price.
rules.fix: One hero figure at most, with the final value in accessible text and the animated digits aria-hidden. Prices never animate.

rules.title: Cursor-tilt and magnetic elements
rules.description: Cards tilt in 3D toward the pointer, or buttons pull toward the cursor.
rules.whyAI: vanilla-tilt and magnetic buttons are gallery effects copied into generated sites. They make targets move while the user aims at them.
rules.heuristic: data-tilt attributes, vanilla-tilt or atropos scripts, or pointermove handlers writing rotateX/rotateY or translate on controls.
rules.fix: Targets stay still under the pointer. Use the depth button hover (1px lift, 4% brighter) and the press scale.

rules.title: Animation loops running off screen
rules.description: Canvas, WebGL, Lottie or Rive loops keep rendering when scrolled away or in a background tab.
rules.whyAI: Embeds are pasted with autoplay and no lifecycle. It drains batteries and steals frames from the visible page.
rules.heuristic: requestAnimationFrame callbacks or player.play state continuing while the element is not intersecting or document.visibilityState is hidden.
rules.fix: Start and stop loops with whenVisible() from @brandcloud/motion/dom (IntersectionObserver plus visibilitychange). Render one static frame for reduced motion.

rules.title: Letter-by-letter or blur-in headline
rules.description: Headlines split into letters or words that fade, blur or slide in one by one.
rules.whyAI: Split-text and blur-in reveals are a popular 2025 to 2026 template effect. They delay reading and fragment text for screen readers.
rules.heuristic: A heading with five or more inline children carrying their own animation or transition-delay, or filter: blur() in an entrance keyframe on text.
rules.fix: Headlines appear whole. If a heading must change, cross-fade the whole line.

rules.title: Preloader or splash animation
rules.description: A logo animation, progress counter or curtain that covers the page before content shows.
rules.whyAI: Agency-template preloaders are a premium signal in screenshots and pure waiting time for visitors.
rules.heuristic: A fixed full-viewport element present at load that animates and is removed after a timer.
rules.fix: No preloaders. Ship fast pages; show skeletons only for data that is actually loading.

rules.title: Auto-playing motion with no pause
rules.description: Carousels, tickers, videos or animations that move for more than five seconds with no way to pause.
rules.whyAI: Auto-advance is a default in carousel and marquee components. It fails WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide.
rules.heuristic: An element that changes on a timer for over 5s without a visible pause or stop control and without stopping on hover and focus.
rules.fix: No auto-advance. If something must play, give it a pause button, stop on hover and focus, and do not start under reduced motion.

rules.title: Meaning only available on hover
rules.description: Details, prices or actions that appear only when a card is hovered.
rules.whyAI: Hover reveals look slick in a desktop demo and hide content on touch and from keyboard users.
rules.heuristic: Content with opacity 0 or visibility hidden that becomes visible only through :hover, with no :focus-within or touch equivalent.
rules.fix: Show the content. Hover may add emphasis, never information.

rules.title: Blur and glass entrances
rules.description: Elements arrive by un-blurring (filter: blur to 0) or with animated backdrop blur.
rules.whyAI: Blur-in is a current AI-template signature, and animating blur is one of the most expensive things a browser can paint.
rules.heuristic: Keyframes or transitions on filter: blur() or backdrop-filter for entrances.
rules.fix: Opacity and a small translate (presets.reveal), or nothing.
